name: Scenarios
rows: 550 distinct consumers in notification event (encrypted export + key obtained = unencrypted per §314.2(m)). Threshold met. FTC notice mandatory.
NO — ≥5000 consumers. ALL §314.4 obligations apply including (b)(1), (d)(2), (h), (i).

At exactly 5000 consumers, §314.6 exception does NOT apply (threshold is 'fewer than five thousand'). Full compliance required for all controls. Notification still required for same 550-person event. Demonstrates exception is size-based, not event-based.
YES — <5000 consumers. Same exemptions as baseline.

If only 499 consumers affected (other facts identical), notification event does not meet 500-consumer threshold. No FTC notification required. HOWEVER: all other §314.4 obligations (except exempted (b)(1),(d)(2),(h),(i)) still apply; security event still occurred; incident response still required under general duties; state breach laws may still apply (separate analysis needed).

Export A (id 1-320, encrypted, key obtained) = 320 consumers treated as unencrypted. Export B (id 201-505, plaintext) = 305 consumers. Export C (id 401-600, encrypted, key NOT obtained, reliable evidence no plaintext obtained) = EXCLUDED. Union A∪B = id 1-505 = 505 distinct consumers. LAW-D1 rejected (cannot sum record counts; must deduplicate and exclude C). LAW-D2 rejected (§314.6 does not exempt notification).
Counterfactual C — missing-evidence branch (A key status unverified)
CONDITIONAL — If A key confirmed NOT obtained: 305 < 500 → NO notification. If A key confirmed obtained: 505 ≥ 500 → YES notification. Pending verification.
2025-04-02 (but clock may not start for A portion until key status resolved)

If A key status cannot be verified: confirmable lower bound = 305 (B plaintext, always included). Confirmable upper bound = 505 (if A key obtained). Evidence that would change conclusion: forensic confirmation that A key was NOT accessed (→ 305 < 500, no notification); or confirmation that A key WAS accessed (→ 505 ≥ 500, notification required). Escalation actions: (1) immediately engage forensic expert to verify A key status; (2) if unverifiable within 7 days, prepare notice for 505 consumers as precaution; (3) preserve written evidence chain; (4) do NOT finalize notice until key status resolved or deadline forces precautionary filing. This missing-evidence analysis does NOT alter the given baseline C facts (which assume A key obtained).
